Docs/ Theme development/Customizer

Customizer

Offer theme options under Appearance › Customize with a live preview, and use them in templates.

Appearance › Customize is the WordPress Customizer: Site Identity (title, tagline, logo, site icon), Colors, Menus, Widgets, Homepage Settings, Additional CSS — plus the sections and settings a theme declares. Values are theme mods, stored per theme, so switching themes and back keeps them.

Declare settings

In theme.json:

"customizer": {
  "sections": [
    {"id": "starter_layout", "title": "Layout", "priority": 40, "settings": [
      {"id": "content_width", "label": "Content width", "type": "radio", "default": "normal",
       "choices": {"narrow": "Narrow", "normal": "Normal", "wide": "Wide"}},
      {"id": "show_sidebar", "label": "Show sidebar", "type": "checkbox", "default": true, "body_class": "has-sidebar"},
      {"id": "footer_text", "label": "Footer text", "type": "textarea", "default": ""}
    ]},
    {"id": "starter_colors", "title": "Theme colors", "settings": [
      {"id": "accent", "label": "Accent", "type": "color", "default": "#2271b1", "css_var": "--accent", "transport": "postMessage"}
    ]}
  ]
}
type Control Value
color colour picker #rrggbb
text, textarea text inputs string
number number input number
checkbox checkbox true / false
select, radio choices from choices one of the keys
image media chooser attachment id

Settings in a section named title_tagline appear under Site Identity, like the Classic theme's "Display Site Title" and "Display Tagline" toggles.

Use the values

In templates every theme mod is in .ThemeMods:

<footer class="site-footer">{{with index .ThemeMods "footer_text"}}<p>{{.}}</p>{{end}}</footer>

Two shortcuts save template code:

  • css_var prints the value as a custom property on :root inside wp_head (.Head), so your stylesheet can use var(--accent).
  • body_class adds that class to .BodyClass when the value is truthy (a checkbox). For a select or radio, read .ThemeMods in the template and print your own class.

Live preview

"transport": "postMessage" tells the Customizer to update the preview without reloading: for css_var and body_class settings the core's preview script applies the change itself; for anything else add a script under assets/ that listens for wp.customize('setting_id', …), exactly as a WordPress theme would (see Classic's assets/js/customize-preview.js), and enqueue it in scripts[]; it only does something inside the Customizer frame, where wp.customize exists. Settings without postMessage refresh the preview frame.

What the core provides

  • Site Identity: blogname, blogdescription, custom logo (.CustomLogo renders it with supports.custom-logo sizes), site icon (.SiteIcon).
  • Colors: background_color and the custom-background support.
  • Menus and Widgets panels edit the locations and areas from theme.json.
  • Homepage Settings: latest posts or a static page (show_on_front, page_on_front, page_for_posts).
  • Additional CSS: .CustomCSS, printed inside .Head.

Changes are previewed through a changeset and saved together with Publish; the preview frame is the real site rendered with the unsaved values.
